teacher_info.intro: I am an American English teacher living and working in Japan.  I have taught ESL (English as a Second Language) at companies, public schools, and universities in the Tokyo area for more than 30 years.  I have held the job titles of Foreign Language Instructor, Head Teacher, Assistant Dean, Reading Researcher,  Registrar, Writer,  Editor, Materials Developer, College Instructor, and Seminar Presenter in English. teacher_info.short_signature: I am an American NCAT-certified public secondary education teacher with 31 years TOESL experience.
teacher_info.introduction: I am currently an English Teacher at the most famous night school in Japan. I have been for seven years. It has a million students of all ages in Japan and a million in South Korea. You would probably recognize their name in your native country. I am a former editor and materials developer for them. I worked in its English Speed Reading Division at their world headquarters. I was teacher of teachers there, speaking at seminars and at all their local and regional teachers' meetings, writing a newsletter for English teachers, fielding questions daily over the phone and through e-mail with them, etc. As an Eng. Editor and their in-house speed reading, native English usage expert, my primary job was to write English stories (350+), review and select materials, proofread worksheets, answer English teacher inquiries, and supply materials for publication and update. I was also an English college instructor in their pilot program of English study at two college campuses. I am the author of Daily Expressions for Men. If you tell me you need to practice English in a role-playing situation such as meeting people, getting to know them, eating at a restaurant, going through customs at an airport, buying tickets at a station, getting directions, shopping, bartering to get a discount on a purchase, visiting the doctor, describing your illness, taking a taxi, checking in a hotel at the front desk, or practically any other scenario, I can supply a dialog and vocabulary we can practice so you can master those skills. I even worked at a British English conversation school for three years here. British English is great! So if you need a program for learning English through dialogs or situation-based role playing, take the TOEIC or TOEFL, or practice email writing, I can really help you! Also, if you just need to practice English conversation, improve your business or English reading skills, or improve pronunciation, fluency or reading speed, I can also be of help.

It teaches constructing speeches, conference presentations, preparing Ted Talks, and actually making short reports at office meetings.  These are very important activities in business.   However, at least a third to half of the class time should be relaxed and give some room to a light topical English discussion at the end of the hour in casual English.  Two ways to do this online are by using the 200 life topic "Conversational Questions" chart located at  http://iteslj.org/questions/ for learning question and answer conversation, questions and answers, vocabulary, and phrases; another is by using a good book, not a web page.  It is  very good idiom, phrasal verb, sentence and dialog interchange, word collocation, vocabulary book called  "English Conversation: Practice Makes Perfect" (found in pdf form with its whole series of associated books at https://vk.com/wall-80584764_18000?null) teaches several levels of English conversation and is very understandable. It is my most popular textbook in Japan.  These materials make up the most useful and practical package of English business material.  They make it possible to have discussions and conversations that have in my ESL teaching experience led dozens of IT students to fluency in about 6 months of steady, earnest English study with them and an italki teacher.  This is the course of study I offer IT people.  Most students speak twice as fast and much more confidently at its end.

course_info.trial_description:
Trial Lesson structure:       

        First, we will get to know each other and have a time for questions. Feel free to ask me any question. I look forward to learning about you and your goals. Then, I will briefly explain my lesson structure and teaching method. Next, based on a topic of your interest, I will come up with a dialogue or use a piece from the internet to learn more about you and this topic. Then, we will practice reading this dialogue together and focus on pronunciation. I will then make a Google Document for us to share, listing new vocabulary or grammar structures. We will then make fun sentences together using these words. 

Homework and Tests: 

      Depending on your level of interest, I can create homework and tests to evaluate your progress. But you get to control your learning pace and therefore do not have to take a single test or have any homework if that is your desire. My main focus is to help make learning fun for you so that you will feel motivated to learn more. So if you want a more or less interactive lesson, please let me know. 

About me: 
      I have had over 2 years of teaching experience. I have taught English to Chinese students online for a year and have taught English to Korean students in person for a year. I am extroverted and love meeting new people. I am open to adjusting lessons to better suit you. So let me know if you want to learn English by watching movies, reading books, cooking together, singing, dancing or doing some other activity. I can also speak some Mandarin Chinese and Korean if you need some help in translation. But our main focus, of course, will be communicating in English. I look forward to meeting you!

pro_course_detail.description:

We will mainly focus on pronunciation, speaking, grammar and listening through a dialogue written in Google Documents. If desired, we can also work on spelling and writing. The main goal of this lesson is to help you sound like a native English speaker. I also hope that you will have fun in introducing yourself. I will help you be as creative as you want in your introduction so we can have a lively conversation. I will also change my introduction occasionally in order to make our dialogue more similar to a natural conversation with a native English speaker and to help improve your confidence. 

Teaching materials:

I will be using Google documents so we can share the vocabulary, grammar, and dialogues that we practiced during class. I will also use quizlet, powerpoint, youtube, and other fun learning apps/websites to further your learning. If desired, we can also use books, social media websites, movies, and more.
